paragraphs: Paladin autonomously deploys drones to emergency incidents so that aerial views reach responders before the first unit arrives. A drone launches automatically from the department's dock as soon as an incident is reported. The company states that responders get eyes on scene in under 90 seconds. The platform is meant for departments regardless of city size and integrates with dispatch workflows.

Paladin supplies the drone, the software, the data management platform and the FAA waivers a department needs to operate legally. Its drone for emergency response, the Knighthawk, is made in the United States. The company describes that drone as NDAA approved and autonomous. A partnership with T-Mobile extends how far the drones can travel.

Ferguson PD in Missouri implemented a Drone-as-First-Responder program with Paladin to improve response times and increase situational awareness. Forest Park PD in Georgia deployed the system for aerial visibility across incidents. Murrells Inlet FD in South Carolina uses it for fire, EMS and search operations. Elizabeth PD in New Jersey scaled from a single drone to a fully staffed 24/7 operation. Divy Shrivastava founded the company and has led it since 2018.

quote.text: Paladin autonomously deploys drones to emergency incidents, delivering real-time aerial intelligence before the first unit arrives.
